MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 9, 2018

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Sachs at 5:00 p.m., on January 9, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 4, 2018, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Sachs

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiators; Property: Site "C" located on City-
  owned land directly adjacent to and southeasterly of the City’s Animal Service center
  off Center Drive, and easterly of Saddleback College; Agency Negotiators: City
  Manager Wilberg, City Attorney Curley, Director Lister (all in Housing Advisory
  Capacity); Negotiating Party: RFP Solicitation/term and condition approval under
  negotiation - price and terms.

City Council Minutes  1  January 9, 2018
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:00 p.m., Mayor Sachs recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with all five Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that staff received direction from the City Council in closed
session and the matter will be brought back to the Council, in open session, in the near future.

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Presentation to Former Mayor Bucknum

  Mayor Sachs presented a gavel plaque to Council Member Bucknum to commemorate her
  service as Mayor in 2017.

P2.  Opening Remarks from Mayor Sachs

  Mayor Sachs presented his goals and objectives for 2018.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Robert Breton, M.V.: thanked Council Member Bucknum for serving the City with grace,
distinction, civility and decorum while she was Mayor in 2017. He congratulated Mayor Sachs on
his new position and noted that he has observed him to be a man of wisdom, integrity, good
judgment and someone who has a strong moral compass. Mr. Breton said it will be a banner year
with Mayor Sachs leading the City.

Penny Lambright and Jerry Bryant, M.V.: thanked the Council for their support of Patriots and
Paws and she expressed gratitude to resident Jerry Bryant for donating a vehicle to the
organization. Mr. Bryant said he appreciated the opportunity to give something of value to those
who that are fighting for the country and keeping Americans free and safe.

Dale Rathburn, M.V.: announced that a residential drug rehab facility has opened next door to his
home and up to six people can reside there. He said that the facility violates the City’s zoning
codes since it is an established business with employees coming and going.

Hoiyin Ip, Sierra Club: discussed her interaction with City staff and thanked them for their
willingness to listen to her ideas. She presented additional concepts for environmental programs
in the City such as a Styrofoam ban and a trash reduction campaign.

City Council Minutes  2  January 9, 2018
 Bill Lane, Dana Point: discussed the importance of waste reduction and how trash in the
watersheds impacts the quality of beaches and water in the oceans. He encouraged the City of
Mission Viejo to reduce the use of Styrofoam and single use plastics and to promote compostables.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: stated that she finds it amusing that the word “districting” is not mentioned
in the title of agenda item 9 and that the word “we” is used throughout Attachment B to the staff
report. She asked for clarification on discrepancies in the agenda report and online information.

Gail Reavis, M.V.: stated that the Mayor's goals for the year are wishful-thinking and the Council
needs to stop studying things to death and get back to the “do” part.

Judy Bullockus, M.V.: thanked Council Member Bucknum for her service as Mayor last year and
congratulated Ed Sachs on his appointment and goals for his term as Mayor this year. She read an
excerpt from her daughter Jennifer’s college essay, in which she wrote fondly about growing up
in Mission Viejo.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of December 12, 2017, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated December 1, 2017 in the Amount of $1,038,433.85

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated December 8, 2017 in the Amount of $719,678.16

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Fiscal Year 2016-17 Mission Viejo Housing Authority Annual Report

  Received and filed.

5.  Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo for the Fiscal
  Year Ended June 30, 2017 and related reports

City Council Minutes  3  January 9, 2018
   Received and filed.

6.  Positions Authorized to Execute Local Agency Investment Fund (LAIF) Transactions

  Adopted Resolution No. 18-01 Designating Positions Who Can Authorize Local Agency
  Investment Fund Transactions.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority Positions Authorized to Execute Local Agency
  Investment Fund (LAIF) Transactions

  Adopted Mission Viejo Housing Authority Resolution 18-01 Designating Positions Who
  Can Authorize Local Agency Investment Fund Transactions.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

PUBLIC HEARINGS

8.  Appeal filed by Darin Blindell of Valuerock MV Properties, LLC (property owner),
  of the Planning and Transportation Commission’s approval of Minor Modification
  MM2017-421, a petition submitted by CenterPoint Integrated Solutions, agent for
  Floor & Décor, to permit site and building modifications to accommodate a new Floor
  & Décor retail business at 25872 Muirlands Boulevard, in the CC (Commercial
  Community) zone. Specifically, the Appeal is of Condition Nos. 8 and 13, of Planning
  and Transportation Commission Resolution No. 2017-1367A, addressing approved
  hours for store delivery and customer pick-up

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  At the hour of 7:03 p.m., Mayor Sachs opened the public hearing.

  On behalf of the Appellant, the following presented information on the Floor & Décor
  project and the conditions that they seek to modify: Amanda Steinle, Centerpoint Integrated
  Solutions; Edward Costa, Floor & Décor; Heather Bruck, Bridgenet Engineering; and
  Patrick Cox, ValueRock Realty Partners.

  The following expressed opposition to the extension of delivery hours and/or the project
  as a whole: Cathy Schlicht, M.V.; Mike Karn, M.V.; Kevin Webb, M.V.; Joseph Romero,
  M.V.; and Tom Smith, M.V.

  The following presented written comments in opposition to extension of the delivery hours
  and/or the location of the Floor & Décor: Edmund Olszowka, M.V.; Misty Webb, M.V.;
  Danean MacAndrew, M.V.; Bruce Mayall, M.V.; Glen Heiman, M.V. Sheryl Heiman,
  M.V.; Shirley Kitaudhi-Smith, M.V.; Joshua Saylor, M.V.; Carolyn Saylor, M.V.; and Jane
  Moss, M.V.

  Mayor Sachs closed the public hearing at 7:48 p.m.

City Council Minutes  4  January 9, 2018
   The Council Members announced the names of the residents and business owners/
  representatives they have interacted with prior to this public hearing.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to affirm
  the Planning and Transportation Commission’s action by approving Resolution 18-02
  Denying the Appeal Petition, and Thereby Approving Minor Modification MM2017-421
  as Approved by the Planning and Transportation Commission, with the following changes
  to Condition Nos. 8 and 13: (1) extend the customer pick-up time to 6:00 p.m.; (2) maintain
  the store delivery time to 5:00 p.m. except on Tuesdays and Thursdays, when store delivery
  time is extended to 6:00 p.m.; and (3) direct staff to review the proposed relocation of the
  pickup door and bring a confirming resolution to the City Council at the next meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell and Kelley
  NOES:  Raths and Sachs
  ABSENT:  None

9.  California Voting Rights Act Mapping Opportunities and Continued Request for
  Public Input

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Mayor Sachs opened the public hearing at 9:00 p.m.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: stated that the process is corrupt and the City is barely meting the
  statutory requirements.

  Joe Tully, M.V.: said that he doesn't see the value in breaking up the City and creating
  districts. He encouraged the Council to evaluate ethnic diversity throughout City.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: stated that the City of Mission Viejo has not discriminated against any
  protected class citizens in its elections and two former Latino Council Members prove his
  point. He said the proposed map is blatantly gerrymandered to allow each of the current
  Council Members their own district.

  Robert Reidel, M.V.: encouraged the City to take this matter to court because he likes the
  status quo with the City’s at-large elections. Mr. Reidel said districts would disenfranchise
  the voters and Capistrano Unified School District’s districts are a good example of how it
  can go wrong.

  Gail Reavis, M.V.: said that proposed map protects the five City Council Members by
  giving them each their own district, even if it meant looping the boundary lines around.
  She said the public needs to see this map and know what is being proposed.

City Council Minutes  5  January 9, 2018
   The following submitted comments in opposition to district elections and the first draft
  map: Dale Rathburn, M.V.; and Kevin Webb, M.V.

  The Council took no action and Mayor Sachs closed the public hearing at 9:18 p.m.

OLD BUSINESS

10.  Prop 1B Audit Corrective Action Plan

  Administrative Services Manager Susan Knudson presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 18-03 Amending FY 17/18 Budget for CIP 837 Arterial Highway Resurfacing
  and CIP 838 Residential Resurfacing in the amount of $45,574.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

11.  City Council Committee and Regional Board/Committee  Representative
  Appointments and Update Posting of FPPC Form 806 Online

  (1) Mayor Sachs recommended representatives and alternates to the following regional
  boards/committees and the City Council voted as indicated:

  Motion made by Mayor Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to appoint Ed
  Sachs as the City’s representative on the Orange County Fire Authority Board of Directors.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  Sachs

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to appoint
  Ed Sachs as the City’s representative on the Transportation Corridor Agencies Board of
  Directors.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  Sachs

City Council Minutes  6  January 9, 2018
   Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to appoint
  Trish Kelley as the City’s alternate on the Transportation Corridor Agencies Board of
  Directors.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  Kelley

  (2) Mayor Sachs appointed members to the existing City of Mission Viejo Committees
  (direct appointments by the Mayor, no vote required):

  (a) CUSD Ad Hoc Committee: Wendy Bucknum and Trish Kelley
  (b) Standing Economic Development Committee: Brian Goodell and Ed Sachs
  (c) Marguerite Aquatics Complex Oversight Ad Hoc Committee: Wendy Bucknum and
  Greg Raths
  (d) Confirming Interim Zoning Ordinance Ad Hoc Committee: Brian Goodell and Ed

  (e) Mission Viejo Olympics Committee: Brian Goodell, Robert Breton, Jerry Henberger,
  Jim Montrella and Greg Raths
  (f) Integrated Solid Waste Services Ad Hoc Committee: Kelley & Sachs

  (3) Mayor Sachs appointed representatives and alternates to the following regional
  boards/committees (direct appointments by the Mayor, no vote required):

  (a) California Joint Powers Insurance Authority: Trish Kelley and Cheryl Dyas
  (b) League of California Cities and Association of California Cities, Orange County:
  Ed Sachs and Greg Raths
  (c) Orange County Council of Governments General Assembly: Brian Goodell and Trish

  (d) Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) General Assembly:
  Wendy Bucknum and Trish Kelley
  (e) Southern Orange County Watershed Management Area Executive Committee: Trish
  Kelley and Brian Goodell
  (f) Oversight Board Robert Breton and Cheryl Dyas
  (g) Orange County Vector Control Board: Robert Ruesch.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths to adopt
  Resolution 18-04 Affirming the Mayor’s Selection and Appointment of Two Members to
  the Oversight Board [item (f) above] Pursuant to California Health and Safety Code,
  Division 24, Part 1.85, Section 34179.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  7  January 9, 2018
   (4) The City Council directed the City Clerk to update the appointees list as required by
  law on Form 806 and post that form to the City's website.

STAFF REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

12.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum referred to the public speaker earlier who was asking about sober living
homes in the Stoneridge Community. She said she was also contacted by a Board Member from
the Stoneridge Homeowner’s Association who asked why the City cannot put a stay on sober living
homes like the City of Laguna Niguel did. Council Member Bucknum requested that staff explore
what Laguna Niguel implemented and whether or not there is an opportunity for Mission Viejo to
do something similar.

City Manager Wilberg noted that several staff members have spoken to the resident and assured
him that the City will take whatever action is available within the confines of the law.

Council Member Bucknum shared that she had a quiet couple of weeks and a nice holiday break.
She congratulated Mayor Sachs on a good job chairing the meeting and said she looks forward to
a great year ahead and to seeing his goals come to fruition. She also asked the Mayor to make sure
that Mission Viejo is protected in relation to traffic and toll road extensions.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell added his congratulations to former Mayor Bucknum for a job well done
last year. He said he admires her work ethic, commitment to the community, and how hard she
worked. He also wished Mayor Sachs and Mayor Pro Tem Raths the best of luck and wisdom in
leading the City Council this year.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley congratulated the City’s new police Chief, Lieutenant Quyen "Q" Vuong
and said she is delighted to see him back in Mission Viejo. She worked with him in the past when
he was a deputy in Mission Viejo and she highlighted the fact that Lieutenant Q developed Text-
a-Tip to provide students with the ability to send anonymous information to School Resource
Officers. Council Member Kelley thanked former Mayor Bucknum for her service last year. She
noted that it is a lot of work to be the Mayor and Wendy did a great job and attended almost every
City and community event. She said she is also pleased to see a snapshot of the upcoming year
City Council Minutes  8  January 9, 2018
 with Mayor Sachs and she knows he'll do a fantastic job as Mayor. Council Member Kelley
thanked the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for their work in planning and staffing Santa's
Workshop during the four weeks leading up to Christmas. In closing, Council Member Kelley
announced that the Community of Character word of the month is perseverance and she provided
examples of some people who have succeeded by persevering.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths welcomed Chief Q to the community and said he likes the idea of more
Sheriff’s patrols throughout the city. He thanked Council Member Bucknum for a great job as
Mayor last year and said he is looking forward to working with Mayor Sachs this year.

Mayor Sachs

Mayor Sachs welcomed and deferred his time to the new Lieutenant, Q Vuong.

Lt. Vuong thanked the City Council and staff for giving him the opportunity to serve Mission Viejo
as the new Chief of Police Services. He said he feels like he is returning home and wants to pay it
forward by growing the new generation of Deputy Sheriffs. Lt. Q said he will maintain a strong
social media presence and invited the Council and residents to follow Mission Viejo Police
Services on Instagram, Twitter, Facebook and Nextdoor. He shared his plans to be out in the City,
reaching out to faith-based communities and the schools; to also show residents that the Orange
County Sheriff’s Department officers are friendly, engaged and will listen and make a difference.
Lt. Q said it is his goal to take police services to the next level and he looks forward to working
with the Council, staff and community.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:59 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Sachs adjourned the meeting in memory of his grandson, Sydney Cohen, to Friday, January
12, 2018, at 6:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of January 23, 2018

City Council Minutes  9  January 9, 2018
